findings.claim: The lock-based match compares the apm.yml git: URL with a lock URL that APM 0.33.0 does not record. For a git-URL dependency the lock splits the source: repo_url is only owner/repo (o/kmctl), with host (127.0.0.1) and port (46239) in separate fields, and no scheme or .git suffix. Dropping the scheme, .git, trailing slash and case from http://127.0.0.1:PORT/o/kmctl.git gives 127.0.0.1:PORT/o/kmctl, which never equals o/kmctl, so the local-source entry is never recognised and the bug stays. LockDependency also has no host or port fields. The plan must build the lock side as host[:port]/repo_url, add those fields, and say so in r1, whose test fixture would otherwise use a made-up full URL in repo_url and pass while the real flow fails.

The plan does not say what happens to remove_old_apm_entry. _names_old_package already matches a {git: ...jasperhg90/knowledge-management..., path: apm} mapping, so in the reverse direction (default source first, then a fork or local --source) install runs apm uninstall JasperHG90/Knowledge-management/apm before write_manifest gets the entry. No spike shows that this uninstall removes a git-URL mapping (spike:apm-only-install/6 used the shorthand string entry). If it doesn't, install raises PluginError and never reaches the new replace-in-place code. The plan should either stop _names_old_package matching the new {git, path: apm} form, leaving write_manifest to handle it, or settle it with a spike: after an install with the default source, does apm uninstall JasperHG90/Knowledge-management/apm remove the {git: https://github.com/JasperHG90/Knowledge-management.git, path: apm} entry from apm.yml?
The lock gives repo_url as owner/repo with host and port apart, so a plain URL comparison never matched a local or fork source.
In the reverse order, remove_old_apm_entry ran apm uninstall on kmctl's own default-source mapping, which no spike shows works.
